title: Drug overdose in police custody accidental, inquest rules
article: A coroner's inquest ruled Thursday the death of a 35-year-old Kelowna, B.C., man in police custody was accidental.
A Kelowna RCMP officer testified Michael Stein swallowed two grams of crack cocaine in the back of a police car last August in an attempt to hide the drugs.
Stein's mother, Lynn Kilroe, said her son likely swallowed the drugs by mistake.
"He was trying to not go to jail. He wanted to chew it up and spit it out, and probably swallowed some of it," she said.
The RCMP officer called an ambulance but told them it was not an emergency.
Stein was eventually taken to the Kelowna RCMP detachment, where police video shows Stein lying on the floor asking for help and complaining the cocaine was still stuck in his mouth.
Eight minutes later, the ambulance arrived, and took Stein to Kelowna General Hospital, where he died nine days later.
Stein's family believes he should have been taken to hospital immediately.
"They're saying that's not their policy, but maybe they should make it their policy," Kilroe said.
The coroner's jury ruled Stein's death, a cocaine-induced heart attack, was an accident.
It made no recommendations, saying there was nothing police and paramedics could have done to prevent his death.
